taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT is Saturday, October 31, 2026 at 8:59 AM in Madrid (CEST, UTC+2).

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles is on Pacific Daylight Time (UTC-7) on October 30, 2026, while Madrid is on Central European Time (UTC+1). So Madrid is 8 hours ahead.

“Coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time” is Monday, November 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM in Los Angeles, which is 6:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 18:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 in Madrid. Exactly 48 hours later is Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00 in Madrid local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT is 19:00 in Madrid, Spain (CET, UTC+1). Adding exactly 72 hours gives October 29, 2026 at 19:00 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CET in late October 2026, since daylight saving time ends that weekend.  
The contest closes at 2026-10-31 23:59 ET; ET is UTC−4 then, so that is 2026-11-01 03:59 UTC.  
Add 36 hours → 2026-11-02 15:59 UTC. Madrid is UTC+1 then, so the announcement is at 16:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp 1791788340 corresponds to **2026-08-12 16:39 UTC**. Tokyo is **UTC+9**, so the local deadline is:

ANSWER: 2026-08-13 01:39 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on 2026-10-25, so the UTC deadline converts to 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026 is **2026-10-25 23:59 PDT**. Madrid is on **CET/CEST** by then, and on that date Madrid is **CEST (UTC+2)** while Pacific Time is **PDT (UTC−7)**, so Madrid is **9 hours ahead**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The U.S. ends daylight saving time in 2026 on **Sunday, November 1, 2026**. At that moment, Eastern Time is still on daylight saving time just before the switch, so **12:00 noon Eastern Time** on that date is **11:00 a.m. in Lima, Peru** (Peru is UTC-5 year-round; Eastern Time is UTC-4 during DST).

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 11:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“24:00 AoE” means the very end of December 31, 2026 in Anywhere on Earth time, which is UTC−12. Tokyo is UTC+9, so that is 21 hours ahead.

So the deadline in Tokyo is:

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is on AEDT on October 5, 2026, which is UTC+11, and New York is on EDT, UTC-4. So New York is 15 hours behind Sydney.

5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 = 2:00 AM in New York on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).
